newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. surgeon warns Yeltsin not to go too fast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. surgeon warns Yeltsin not to go too fast.

text.p: Veteran U.S. cardiologist Michael Debakey said on Wednesday that things were going well after Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation, but he warned the president not to take things too fast.

"Everything is going quite well and of course it is very gratifying to see this happen because this is a very good sign that his prognosis is excellent," DeBakey, who was a consultant during Tuesday's operation, told CNN television. He added: "I told him (this morning) you must be very patient."
"I said -- You must be very patient, because I know that you want to get going. But I said - You know its very important that you follow the doctors' instructions," DeBakey said.
DeBakey said there were several possible complications for a heart patient after surgery, including bleeding, but added: "Fortunately none of them are taking place right now".

He said Yeltsin, who was alert and smiling when he saw him on Wednesday morning, might be able to return to nearly full-time work in six to eight weeks and could even play tennis in up to four months.
The 88-year-old U.S. surgeon who performed the world's first bypass operation, praised his pupil, Russian cardiologist Renat Akchurin, who led the operating team.
